articles.title: General strike in Greece rejects militarization and austerity
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: A nationwide general strike in Greece drew tens of thousands onto the streets of approximately 80 towns and cities on Wednesday, November 25. Workers from both the public and private sectors protested against further austerity and war spending. “We refuse to pay with our lives and incomes for involvement in war and the profits of business groups,” the All-Workers Militant Front (PAME) stated when announcing the strike. The strike call had already been launched during the dockworkers’ international day of action against the militarization of ports at the end of October. It is expected to ripple outward in the coming weeks, including during a new national mobilization on December 15. articles.title: “Huna”: Egyptian Author Abdelrahman ElGendy on Prison, National Book Award & Being Denied U.S. Visa
articles.content_excerpt: This year’s annual National Book Award ceremony in New York City was marked by the notable absence of nonfiction winner Abdelrahman ElGendy, after the Trump administration denied the Egyptian author entry into the United States. articles.title: If You Want to Win, Learn to Think From Other People’s Perspective
articles.author: Chris Brooks
articles.content_excerpt: A Necker cube does something interesting if you look at it long enough. The image stays the same, but the cube suddenly flips. One minute the left side looks closest to you, then the next moment it looks further away. The underlying facts never change. The lines remain exactly in the same place. What changes is how you perceive those lines. Differences in perspective come up all the time… Source

articles.title: Japan to revise national security policy, weaken postwar non-nuclear commitments
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) claimed on Monday, November 23, that it will revise the country’s three security documents by the end of the year and possibly acquire nuclear-power submarines soon. Civil society groups on China and Japan have been opposing the decision, calling it a move towards remilitarization. They also claim such a move would be disastrous for regional peace and security and for the post-war regional order. Keitaro Ohno, a leader of the LDP and a member of Japanese parliament reportedly reiterated that Japan has rejected the proposal to get a nuclear-powered submarine in the wake of strong popular opposition and objections raised by China. articles.title: Gaza declares epidemic alert after meningitis claimed 15 lives
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: On Tuesday, November 24, the Ministry of Health in the Gaza Strip declared an “epidemic alert” across all governorates, after 1,790 meningitis cases were recorded, adding that at least 15 people had died from the infectious disease. The ministry warned of an increase in fatalities due to meningitis, particularly among children. It attributed the surge in cases to the repercussions of Israel’s genocidal aggression against Gaza and its continued ban on the entry of medicine and other essential supplies into the war-ravaged territory. articles.title: Israeli forces raid Al-Ama’ri Refugee Camp, detain dozens of Palestinians
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: On Monday, November 23, the Israeli military stormed Al-Ama’ri refugee camp in Al-Bireh city in the central occupied West Bank. During the hours-long raid, Israeli forces converted the Al-Ama’ri Youth Center, alongside several residential homes, into temporary detention and field interrogation sites. They also damaged the facilities of the center. 30 Palestinians were briefly detained and interrogated after their homes were raided, but were released before the military left the camp. However, one Palestinian young man was arrested in the assault, during which stun grenades and tear gas were fired.
